13	## Lexer protocol
14	
15	`from minisql.lexer import Token, tokenize`; `tokenize(sql: str) -> list[Token]` lexes the whole string, including a terminal EOF token. `KEYWORDS` is the exact reserved set, a frozenset of uppercase strings; aggregate function names remain ordinary identifiers.
16	
17	`Token` is a frozen dataclass with fields, in order:
18	
19	| Field | Meaning |
20	|---|---|
21	| kind | `INT`, `REAL`, `STRING`, `IDENT`, `QUOTED_IDENT`, `EOF`, an uppercase keyword, or the operator/punctuation itself |
22	| raw | Exact token source spelling, including any quotes |
23	| value | int/float for numbers; decoded str for names/strings; uppercase str for keywords; raw symbol for punctuation; None for EOF |
24	| start, end | Zero-based code-point offsets, end-exclusive |
25	| line, column | One-based token-start coordinates; only LF splits lines |
26	
27	In particular, a NULL token is a keyword token whose value is `"NULL"`; consumers derive the NULL literal's type/value from its kind, not from token.value. `007` decodes to int 7, `1e2` to float 100.0. Quoted names retain their case in decoded value; resolution later uses lower(), not casefold(). Unicode is accepted inside quotes, not in unquoted ASCII identifiers or numbers. Numeric continuation checking is ASCII as specified in feature-specification.md §5.2. Comments end only at LF. EOF has raw `""`, value None, start=end=len(sql), and the position immediately after all input, including trailing whitespace/comments.
28	
29	## Parser entry and ownership boundary
30	
31	`from minisql.parser import parse`; `parse(sql: str) -> minisql.ast.Query` fully tokenizes before constructing the parser, so LexError anywhere in the input precedes a possible ParseError. No catalog, name/function resolution, static typing, execution, or output formatting occurs here. For example, unknown function names, non-COUNT star calls, and multi-character literal ESCAPEs parse and await semantic validation.
32	
33	All AST records are frozen dataclasses, with inherited `start: int, end: int` fields first. Spans are code-point offsets into `Query.source`, end-exclusive. All sequence fields below are tuples. Optional tokens/nodes use None. All name/alias/operator/star/ESCAPE fields below are original lexer Token objects, not rewritten strings.
34	
35	### Expressions (`minisql.ast.Expr` subclasses)
36	
37	- `Literal(start, end, token)`: INT/REAL/STRING/NULL; token.kind preserves static literal kind and token.value preserves decoded numeric/string values.
38	- `Column(start, end, name, qualifier)`: name Token and optional qualifier Token. A qualified reference starts at its qualifier. Both IDENT and QUOTED_IDENT are accepted.
39	- `Unary(start, end, operator, operand)`: unary +/- or prefix NOT. The operator is its exact token.
40	- `Binary(start, end, left, operator, right)`: arithmetic, comparisons, AND, OR. Keyword operator kinds are uppercase, raw spelling remains unchanged; != and <> remain distinct.
41	- `IsNull(start, end, operand, operator, not_token, null_token)`: operator is IS, optional not_token is NOT.
42	- `Like(start, end, operand, operator, pattern, not_token, escape_keyword, escape)`: operator is LIKE even for NOT LIKE; escape_keyword is ESCAPE and escape is its STRING token. Runtime LIKE errors belong at operator; invalid ESCAPE length belongs at escape.
43	- `In(start, end, operand, operator, items, not_token, lparen, rparen)`: operator is IN even for NOT IN; items is a nonempty tuple of full expressions.
44	- `Call(start, end, name, argument, star, lparen, rparen)`: exactly one of argument Expr or star Token is present. Name is an ordinary or quoted name token. COUNT(*)'s star position is available directly.
45	- `Parenthesized(start, end, expression, lparen, rparen)`: explicit wrapper, including nested wrappers, with its own outer span. Parentheses are not erased during parsing.
46	
47	Precedence is unary signs > multiplicative > additive > one comparison/predicate > recursive NOT > left-associative AND > left-associative OR. Comparisons cannot chain without explicit parentheses; failure is at the second operator. Calls take one expression or star; IN has at least one expression. LIMIT/OFFSET take INT tokens, never signed, real, or parenthesized expressions.
48	
49	### Query and surrounding records
50	
51	- `Wildcard(start, end, star, qualifier)`: a Node, not an Expr; star Token and optional qualifier Token for bare * or q.*. Only projection items accept it.
52	- `SelectItem(start, end, expression, alias, as_token)`: expression is Expr or Wildcard; alias and as_token are optional name/AS tokens. Explicit AS and implicit aliases remain distinguishable. A SelectItem span includes its alias when present, while its expression span never includes that alias. Wildcards have no alias production.
53	- `TableRef(start, end, name, alias, as_token)`: name/alias Tokens; effective range name is alias if present, else name. TableRef span includes its alias.
54	- `Join(start, end, kind, table, condition, keyword, join_token, outer_token, on_token)`: kind is `INNER` for JOIN/INNER JOIN, `LEFT` for LEFT [OUTER] JOIN. keyword is the first JOIN/INNER/LEFT token; join_token is JOIN; outer_token exists only for LEFT OUTER JOIN; on_token is ON. condition is a complete Expr.
55	- `OrderItem(start, end, expression, direction)`: optional ASC/DESC Token; None means ASC. Span includes a direction if present; expression span does not.
56	- `Query(start, end, source, select_token, distinct, items, from_table, joins, where, group_by, having, order_by, limit, offset, semicolon)`: source is the entire original sql string. distinct is its DISTINCT Token or None. items is a nonempty SelectItem tuple. from_table is optional; joins are in source order. where/having are optional expressions. group_by and order_by are tuples, empty when absent. limit/offset are optional unsigned INT Tokens; use `.value` for the integer. semicolon is its optional token. Query span runs from SELECT through the last syntactic token, including a semicolon when present but excluding trailing comments/whitespace. EOF consumes all remaining input; only one semicolon is accepted.
57	
58	## Source metadata rules for T4
59	
60	1. Explicit output alias: `item.alias.value`, preserving query spelling without quotes.
61	2. Unparenthesized column: only a direct `isinstance(item.expression, ast.Column)` qualifies for its resolved CSV header. Parenthesized(Column) does not qualify.
62	3. Otherwise derive heading by `query.source[item.expression.start:item.expression.end]`. This retains case, spaces, comments, multiline strings, and parentheses without including aliases or surrounding whitespace.
63	4. Bare ORDER ordinal: expression must be a direct Literal with `token.kind == "INT"`. Parenthesized(1), unary +1, and REAL 1.0 are not bare ordinals.
64	5. Bare ORDER alias candidate: expression must be a direct Column with qualifier None. Parenthesized names and qualified names are ordinary input expressions.
65	6. For resolved structural identity, unwrap Parenthesized recursively; ignore spans/token spelling; preserve literal kind plus decoded value, operator kind/symbol identity, operand order, and resolved column identities. Do not conflate != and <> or use the heading as a structural key. This normalization belongs to T4, not the parser.
66	7. Operator errors use the operator Token; qualified-column errors use the qualifier Token when present, otherwise name. Duplicate range-name errors use the second TableRef.alias or TableRef.name. Group/condition expression starts can be mapped from their start offsets into Query.source; the original first token remains available through the expression's fields.
